calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Dubois and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Flyers’ first line is Martone, Cates and Michkov.

story.head: Strome has three assists as the Capitals beat the Flyers
paras: Alex Tuch struck first for the Capitals just under two minutes in, but Sean Couturier tied it up for Philadelphia early in the second. Jordan Kyrou put the Capitals back ahead 2-1 on the power play less than three minutes later. Aliaksei Protas stretched the lead to 3-1 late in the second. Matvei Michkov cut Washington’s lead to 3-2 on the power play midway through the third, but that was as close as they got. Kyrou scored his second of the night with just over seven minutes left to make it 4-2 for the Caps. Tuch struck again into the empty net with less than three minutes left. Jack St. Ivany made his Capitals debut, after starting the season with the Jets, and picked up two assists. Dylan Strome finished with three assists.

The Capitals had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Flyers 30-25. Logan Thompson made 23 saves for the Capitals, and Joseph Woll stopped 25 of 29 at the other end. The Capitals moved to 7-4-0 and climbed to fourth in the Metropolitan, while the Flyers fell to 3-8-4, still last in the Metropolitan.
